summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga was an Indology, Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki at Kyoto University, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1930, 1950) and as president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan.
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 1990 and as a professor in 2014.

Atul Chandra Chatterjee worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University under Charles Henry Tawney, and at King's College, Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1897 to 1931.

August Blau specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under August Friedrich Pott and Carl Cappeller, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He held posts at Wrocław and Göttingen university libraries, and became librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1892.

August Boeckh worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher, and held posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).
August Clemens Schoener was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued theology studies at the University of Munich and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between 1890 and 1894.

August Conrady was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. under Julius Jolly at Würzburg and habilitated at Leipzig, where he taught from 1891, becoming director in 1914 and professor in 1920. He also taught at Peking University.
August Constantin Boltz was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena around 1843–1845 and served as a professor at the Prussian Military Academy from 1852 to 1864.

August Dillmann worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald, Rudolf von Roth, and August Schleicher. He served as professor at Tübingen (1853), Kiel (1854), Giessen (1864–1869), and Humboldt University of Berlin from 1869.

August Ferdinand Naeke specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1805 to 1809 and held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1811–1818) and the University of Bonn (circa 1818–1838).

August Fick was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Karl Friedrich Hermann, and Heinrich Ewald, later serving there as professor (1876) before becoming ordinary professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Fischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg, held a post at the University of Leipzig from circa 1900 to 1930, and served on the board of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

August Friedrich Pott specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen under Karl Otfried Müller and Thomas Christian Tychsen, and at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Wilhelm von Humboldt. He held a professorship at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and history. He studied at the Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian Theological College, under Karl Rudolf Marx, and at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he served as privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925).

August Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Uppsala and completed his Ph.D. under William Dwight Whitney at Yale. He held academic posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Gothenburg, and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

August Johan Bernet Kempers was an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, directed Dinas Purbakala (1947–1956) and the Netherlands Open Air Museum (1958–1970), and was extraordinary professor at the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as a professor of Slavic philology and linguistics at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

August Ludwig von Schlözer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University around 1755–1756 and held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1769 to 1809.

August Schleicher was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and held professorships at the University of Bonn, Charles University, and the University of Jena.
August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who is a PhD student at Ghent University, where he is attested from 2024 through 2026.
